facts.fact: Roughly 89.3% of US households own at least one internet-connected TV device, according to eMarketer data cited by StackAdapt.
facts.quote: roughly [89.3% of US households](https://forecasts-na1.emarketer.com/584b26021403070290f93a3a/5851918a0626310a2c1869b5) owning at least one internet-connected TV device

facts.fact: CTV streaming is projected to reach 248 million US viewers by 2027, according to eMarketer data cited by StackAdapt.
facts.quote: CTV streaming projected to reach [248 million US viewers](https://forecasts-na1.emarketer.com/584b26021403070290f93a3a/5851918a0626310a2c1869b8) by 2027

facts.fact: According to Business Insider, CTV ad minutes per hour grew 18% across streaming platforms including Netflix, Prime Video, and Paramount+ between January and August 2026.
facts.unit: % growth in CTV ad minutes per hour
facts.quote: CTV ad minutes per hour grew 18% across streaming platforms including Netflix, Prime Video, and Paramount+ between January and August 2026

facts.fact: StackAdapt recommends providing a brand hook within the first three seconds of a CTV ad when the campaign objective is awareness and reach.
facts.quote: Provide a brand hook within the first three seconds.

facts.fact: StackAdapt suggests that existing creative can be adapted for CTV by editing ads down to 15- or 30-second clips.
facts.quote: editing ads down to 15- or 30-second clips

facts.fact: StackAdapt notes that some publishers do not allow QR codes in ad creative.
facts.quote: some publishers don’t allow them in ad creative

facts.fact: StackAdapt recommends that CTV ads earn viewers' focus with an attention-grabbing opening hook within the first three to five seconds.
facts.quote: earns viewers’ focus in the first three to five seconds. Use eye-catching visuals, movement, and captivating audio cues

facts.fact: StackAdapt advises that a viewer should be able to understand a CTV ad's main message within 15 or 30 seconds, without prior brand knowledge.
facts.quote: A viewer should be able to understand the main message within 15- or 30-seconds.

facts.fact: StackAdapt advises introducing the brand within the first three to five seconds of a CTV ad.
facts.quote: Introduce your brand within the first three to five seconds.

facts.fact: StackAdapt states that 15-second and 30-second formats account for the vast majority of CTV inventory.

facts.fact: In an EMARKETER analysis of display, video, and CTV ads, ads that grew brand attention used a slogan at the end of the ad 74% of the time.
facts.quote: ads that grew brand attention used a slogan at the end of an ad 74% of the time.

facts.fact: In the same EMARKETER analysis, high-performing CTV ads used distinct colors 63% of the time.
facts.quote: distinct colors (63% of the time)

facts.fact: In the same EMARKETER analysis, high-performing CTV ads used a distinct ad style 42% of the time.
facts.quote: distinct ad style (42%)

facts.fact: In the same EMARKETER analysis, high-performing CTV ads used package shape as a distinct brand element 32% of the time.
facts.quote: package shape (32%)

facts.fact: In the same EMARKETER analysis, high-performing CTV ads used representations of distinct tastes, textures, and scents 21% of the time.
facts.quote: representations of distinct tastes, textures, and scents (21%)

facts.fact: StackAdapt recommends limiting the number of supporting proof points to one or two behind a single primary CTV message.
facts.quote: support it with one or two supporting proof points

facts.fact: StackAdapt recommends introducing a brand hook within the first three seconds of a CTV spot.
facts.quote: Introduce a brand hook within the first three seconds, and deliver clear audio and visual branding throughout the spot.

facts.fact: StackAdapt states that flashing a QR code for two seconds at the end of a spot is not going to be effective, so CTAs need more time for viewers to act.
facts.quote: Flashing a QR code for two seconds right at the end of a spot isn’t going to be effective.

facts.fact: StackAdapt's Creative Studio lead Israel recommends A/B testing underperforming CTV campaigns by trimming video lengths from 30 to 15 seconds.
facts.quote: Trimming video lengths from 30 to 15 seconds

facts.fact: StackAdapt suggests comparing a 15-second ad edit against a 30-second edit as an example of a single-variable CTV creative test.
facts.quote: comparing a 15-second edit to a 30-second edit

facts.fact: Most CTV ads are either 15 or 30 seconds in length, according to StackAdapt.
facts.quote: Most CTV ads are either 15- or 30-seconds in length.

facts.fact: StackAdapt recommends testing adjusting video length from 30 seconds to 15 seconds as a variable in underperforming CTV campaigns.
facts.quote: Some recommended variables to test in underperforming campaigns include variations in colors, adjusting video lengths from 30 seconds to 15 seconds

facts.fact: StackAdapt advises testing one variable at a time in CTV creative A/B tests so that a change in performance can be attributed to a specific element.
facts.quote: Test one variable at a time to ensure what element the change in performance is attributed to.

facts.fact: StackAdapt says a QR code is useful in CTV ads when direct action is the goal, and is not necessary when the objective is brand awareness.
facts.quote: If the campaign objective is simply brand awareness, it isn’t necessary to include a QR code.

facts.fact: StackAdapt advises that CTV creative should remain easy to understand in case viewers have the volume turned down or are watching in a noisy environment.
facts.quote: the creative should still be easy to understand in case viewers have the volume turned down or are watching TV in a noisy environment.
